source.title: Cognitive cost as dynamic allocation of energetic resources.

confidence_rationale: This is the single closest paper to Q-080's actual proposal, and it splits the two horns cleanly. It SUPPORTS the 'energy conservation as an evolutionarily-primary drive / least-effort prior' half: the brain is modelled as purposively conserving activity, planning longer-term allocation of a limited metabolic budget (astrocytic glycogen), so a least-effort prior is a first-class control objective, not a derived one. But it WEAKENS the 'effort = harm' framing: conservation is cast as OPTIMAL ALLOCATION of a replenishable buffer, not as damage/irreversible residue -- glycogen depletes AND repletes, with no harm-like special status. So it endorses energy-primacy while explicitly NOT reaching for a harm channel to do it. Confidence 0.6: conceptually on-target and it subsumes both cost/benefit and limited-resource views, but the glycogen-buffer mechanism is a proposal (the authors call the biological basis provisional), and it is a control-theoretic model without direct REE mapping.
failure_signatures: A replenishable energy buffer (glycogen depletes and repletes) supports a least-effort PRIOR without any harm/irreversibility semantics. If REE can get energy-conservation-as-primary-drive from a reversible-budget mechanism, then Q-080's harm-coupling is over-specified: it would wrongly assign irreversible special status to what is actually a reversible resource.

The harm-coupling proposal is only justified where the depletion is genuinely IRREVERSIBLE / damage-like. If, as here, sustained over-use merely draws down a buffer that refills with rest, the correct REE representation is an allostatic-load / opportunity-cost term (already present) plus a least-effort prior -- NOT the harm stream.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Cognitive cost is modelled as the brain purposively conserving activity to manage longer-term allocation of limited metabolic resources. A control-theoretic (optimal-control) model with an energy budget reproduces effort-avoidance as OPTIMAL allocation of limited energetic reserves, and captures both reward-responsiveness and hypoglycemia-induced cognitive decrements. Astrocytic glycogen is proposed as the plausible limited buffer: it can transiently support neural activity beyond the rate blood glucose sustains, and its depletion/repletion dynamics match many cognitive-cost phenomena. The model is offered as SUBSUMING both the cost/benefit (opportunity-cost) and the limited-resource views.
mapping.ree_translation: Q-080 has two horns: (A) energy-conservation weighted as an evolutionarily-PRIMARY drive / least-effort prior, and effort-over-exertion coupled to REE's HARM/allostatic stream with irreversibility-aware special status; versus (B) existing value-subtraction (EVC + opportunity-cost) plus pACC allostatic load already suffices. Christie & Schrater support horn (A)'s energy-PRIMACY component -- energy conservation is a first-class control objective, a genuine least-effort prior -- but they achieve it with a REVERSIBLE budget (glycogen depletes AND repletes), i.e. WITHOUT the harm/irreversibility semantics horn (A) also asks for. So for REE the read is: adopt the least-effort prior / energy-primacy, but represent the depletion as reversible allostatic load (pACC, already present) rather than as harm. That endorses part of the proposal and undercuts the harm-coupling part -- hence mixed.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The glycogen-as-buffer mechanism is explicitly a PROPOSAL the authors flag as provisional in its biological basis, and the model is control-theoretic without primary experimental validation of the specific mechanism. It concerns cognitive/metabolic cost in a reversible-buffer regime; it does not address whether TRULY excessive, damaging over-exertion (rhabdomyolysis-scale, genuinely irreversible) should get harm status -- that extreme is where harm-coupling could still be right and this model is silent. So it discriminates the ordinary energy-conservation regime (reversible -> not harm) but not the pathological extreme.
mapping.source_context: Computational / control-theoretic model with proposed neurophysiological grounding (Frontiers in Neuroscience 2015). Domain: human cognitive neuroscience / metabolic modelling. No new primary data; the glycogen dynamics are drawn from the published literature.

confidence_components.notes: Source quality good -- a well-cited synthesis that explicitly unifies opportunity-cost and limited-resource accounts, which is exactly the terrain Q-080 occupies. Mapping fidelity moderate-good: it is the closest paper to Q-080's own framing and cleanly separates energy-primacy (supported) from harm/irreversibility (not needed). Transfer risk moderate-elevated: the glycogen mechanism is provisional and the model is not experimentally validated for the specific buffer, and it is silent on the pathological-over-exertion extreme where harm-coupling could still hold.
